Subject: Lakeshore launch surge — dedicated capacity ask

Irene,

We’re ramping toward our public beta on 2029-06-10 and have a short window where traffic will spike ~6x for ~3 weeks. Based on early load tests we need a predictable pool of GPUs to avoid throttling inference requests during peak hours.

Can Redwood commit to a temporary dedicated tranche (8 x A100 equivalent) for 3 weeks starting 2029-06-01? We can do a short-term uplift on the reserved commit if needed. Attached: Lakeshore_Commit_Schedule_v2.xlsx (contains projected Q2 token volumes + time windows).

Key asks:
- Firm availability window (start/end) and guaranteed throughput SLA during the tranche
- Price for temporary reserved capacity (3-week uplift) and any minimum fees
- If full tranche unavailable, proposal for a proportional split across our reserved lanes + burst policy

Trevor
VP Product, Lakeshore Analytics

Subject: Re: Lakeshore launch surge — capacity mapping & constraints

Irene/Ben — reviewed the schedule. Summary from infra planning:

Findings:
- 8 x A100-equivalent sustained for 3 weeks is a heavy request given committed Reserved tranches over the same period (we already have 2 medium deals pinned in week 22-24).
- Live maintenance (cluster firmware updates) is scheduled 2029-06-03 -> 2029-06-05 on a portion of the pool; that reduces available spare capacity in the earliest part of the window.

Proposed technical options (ranked):
1) Proportional slice across Lakeshore’s reserved lanes + temporary burst lanes during peak hours (preferred). This keeps baseline latency predictable and distributes load.
2) One-time dedicated tranche of 6 x A100-equivalent (instead of 8) for the full 3 weeks, with guaranteed throughput but limited headroom.
3) If we cannot meet either, shift a portion of traffic to a smaller, cheaper quantized model for non-latency-sensitive calls (fallback).

I’m attaching a slot_request_form.pdf with internal slot identifiers and which racks would be used if option (2) is chosen. Need commercial sign-off for reserve billing and a final concurrency number from Lakeshore to compute exact token budgets.

Markus
Principal Infra Planner, Redwood Inference

Trevor — thanks for the transparency. Commercial summary and asks:

Proposals:
- Option A (Preferred): Proportional allocation across your reserved lanes + 2 burst lanes during peak hours (hourly auto-scale to absorb the 6x). Estimated uplift: +30% month-of usage charges, no separate tranche fee. Requires agreement to token caps in the attached spreadsheet.
- Option B: Dedicated short tranche (6 x A100-eq) for 3 weeks. One-time minimum fee = $45k, plus usage. This gives the strongest SLA for p50/p95 latency.
- Option C: Hybrid — 4 dedicated + proportional split for remainder. Reduced fee to $28k.

Commercial constraints: any dedicated uplift needs exec exceptions if it impacts other reserves. Marissa (copied) will need to approve a temporary reallocation for that week.

Next steps I need from Lakeshore:
- Confirmation of Option preference (A/B/C) no later than Mon 2029-05-06 EOD
- Signed amendment or PO (we can provide a short-form amendment)
